Definition: from G4862 and a derivative of a presumed compound of G2095 and a derivative of G2192 (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together:--feast with.
BiblicalUsage: Peter calls the false teachers spots and blemishes, sporting themselves with their own deceivings while they feast with you, and Jude calls them spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear. They sit at the church's table and eat its love feast as if it were their own, and the feasting is the proof of the fraud.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a feast shared with the faithless is no feast at all, and I hold that the church must watch its own table.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
